data.title: Who's building Bengaluru's biggest housing projects? Godrej, Prestige lead
data.description:
Bengaluru’s residential property market is seeing developers launch homes at a scale that could translate into nearly ₹60,000 crore in sales value, with the top 10 players collectively introducing more than 28,000 residential units in the first nine months of 2026.
 
The developers recorded a combined potential sales value of ₹59,336 crore across 28,204 newly launched apartments and villas between January and September 2026, according to an analysis by CRE Matrix.
 
Godrej Properties emerged as the largest developer in the rankings, with a potential sales value of ₹10,362 crore across 4,759 units. Prestige Group followed with ₹9,110 crore across 5,196 units, while Sobha Limited ranked third with ₹7,349 crore across 3,426 units.
 
 
Sumadhura Group secured the fourth position, recording a potential sales value of ₹6,535 crore across 2,781 residential units. Embassy Group rounded off the top five with ₹5,698 crore across 1,730 units.
 
 Top five developers account for nearly two-thirds of value
 
The top five developers together recorded a potential sales value of ₹39,054 crore, accounting for 65.8% of the combined value of the top 10 developers.
 
The concentration is particularly evident at the top of the rankings. Godrej Properties alone accounted for about 17.5% of the total potential sales value, while Sumadhura Group contributed approximately 11%.
 
The remaining five developers in the top 10 were Puravankara and Provident Housing, Assetz Properties Group, Sattva Group, Brigade Group and Lodha Group.
 
Puravankara and Provident Housing ranked sixth with a potential sales value of ₹5,349 crore across 3,805 units. Assetz Properties Group followed with ₹4,935 crore across 2,371 units, while Sattva Group recorded ₹4,568 crore across 1,835 units.
 
Brigade Group and Lodha Group ranked ninth and tenth, with potential sales values of ₹2,776 crore and ₹2,654 crore, respectively.
 
 Prestige leads in number of homes launched
 
While Godrej Properties topped the rankings by potential sales value, Prestige Group launched the highest number of residential units during the period.
 
Prestige introduced 5,196 units, ahead of Godrej Properties’ 4,759 units. Puravankara and Provident Housing also recorded a relatively high launch volume of 3,805 units.
 
The difference between launch volumes and potential sales value reflects the varying scale and estimated value of projects across developers.
 
Across the top 10, the combined potential sales value works out to an average of around ₹2.1 crore per launched unit. This is an aggregate estimate and does not represent the price of an individual home or the average price of homes actually sold.
 
“Bengaluru’s residential real estate market continues to demonstrate significant depth and competitiveness, with the top 10 developers collectively accounting for over ₹59,000 crore in potential sales value through new launches in the first nine months of 2026. Sumadhura Group, which secured the fourth position, accounts for approximately 11% of the combined potential sales value of the top 10 developers. The rankings reflect the competitive nature of Bengaluru’s residential market and the scale at which developers with a strong regional presence are participating in the city’s residential development landscape," said Abhishek Kiran Gupta, Co-Founder & CEO, CRE Matrix.
 
The ₹59,336 crore figure represents the estimated sales value of residential inventory launched during the January-September period. It should not be read as the amount developers have already sold, booked or recognised as revenue.
 
Top 10 developers in Bengaluru by potential sales value (Jan–Sep 2026)
 
Top five developers account for nearly 66% of potential sales value
The analysis covers apartment and villa projects launched in Bengaluru during the period, with developers ranked according to the potential sales value of their newly launched residential projects.
 
The analysis also highlights differences in the scale and value of residential launches across developers. While Prestige Group led in terms of launched supply with 5,196 residential units, Godrej Properties secured the highest potential sales value. The combined implied average potential sales value across the top 10 developers stood at approximately ₹2.10 crore per launched residential unit.

data.title: RBI's first state debt switch success opens door for more auctions: Traders
data.description:
The Reserve Bank of India's first ever ​switch of state government securities saw strong participation from lenders, leading to near full subscription.
 
The strong response has market participants anticipating more rounds of such switch auctions.
 
Indian ‌states sold debt worth around ​₹8,000 crore ($864.63 ​million) and bought back securities worth nearly ₹8,300 crore, the Reserve Bank of India said
 
A switch auction allows the issuer to buy back shorter-term bonds with near-term maturities, while selling longer-dated papers ​at the same time.
 
While the Indian federal ‌government holds switch auctions at least once a ​month, such auctions for state government securities have not taken place before.
 
 
Bonds issued by the states of Madhya ‌Pradesh, Punjab, Rajasthan, Tamil ​Nadu and Uttar Pradesh ‌were swapped at Thursday's auction.
 
"Some banks wanted to let ‌go of the papers that are out of (the) ​money," a trader with a private bank said, replacing them with fresh notes that ​are easier to buy and sell.
 
"We could see more such auctions in the ‌remaining part of the financial year," the trader added.
 
Indian states plan to borrow ₹2.78 trillion through bonds in the October-December quarter of the current fiscal year.

data.title: New Zealand election ends in deadlock as both blocs fall short of majority
data.description:
The final vote count in New Zealand's election published Friday showed neither the right-wing incumbents nor the left-wing opposition bloc won enough seats in Parliament to form a majority government, leaving the prospect of lengthy and fraught negotiations to break the deadlock.

The election on November 7 was the tightest vote in years and didn't deliver a decisive victory for the right or the left, although the conservative bloc finished the night with a wafer-thin majority. But after counting of 4,00,000 so-called special votes, including those cast by New Zealanders living abroad, the Electoral Commission said Friday that the main centre-right party National, led by Prime Minister Christopher Luxon, had lost two seats.

 

That left the right-wing parties with a collective 65 seats in a 130-seat Parliament, with 66 needed for a majority government. The left-wing opposition, led by the Labour party's Chris Hipkins, won 58 seats, up by one from election night.

The figures leave a new entrant to parliament, the Opportunity party - a centrist group that won seven seats, as the deciders of what the shape of the next government will be. While their seven seats wouldn't apparently be enough to propel the left to power, Luxon and his right-wing government partners face lengthy negotiations with Opportunity to form a governing deal.

Opportunity, led by 38-year-old business consultant and political newcomer Qiulae Wong, is unaligned with either bloc and Wong has said she could work with either side to form a government. Wong's pledges of evidence-based centrism and an end to partisan bickering appeared to have appealed to voters, who delivered a stinging rebuke with the result to the major parties, National and Labour, which have long dominated New Zealand politics.

The final count showed more support for minor parties on the ideological flanks than before. A total of 2.8 million votes were cast.

data.title: Urban Company gains 2% on AC biz entry; Voltas, Blue Star, Havells fall
data.description:
Shares of Home-services platform Urban Company gained nearly 2 per cent in early trade on Friday after the company announced its foray into the air conditioner category through its brand Native Ultra and Native Ultra Air ACs
 
The company’s counter at 09:18 AM was trading 0.7 per cent higher at ₹171 per share on NSE. In comparison, Nifty 50 was down 0.08 per cent at 25,605.35. In intraday trade, the stock gained 1.7 per cent to touch the day's high at ₹172.96 per share.
 
Urban Company said that Native AC comes with a five-year unconditional warranty that covers gas refills, meaning zero repair costs for five years, along with a 10-year compressor warranty. The company further added that over the years it has handled more than 18 million AC service and repair jobs. 
 
 
Native AC, priced at ₹55,499 onwards, were made available for pre-booking from November 26, 2026, exclusively on the Urban Company app, with assisted buying available. The full range will be announced at launch.
 
Brokerage firm SBI Securities has given the company a positive rating ‘in the medium to long term’
 
Vipin Kumar, AVP research at Globe Capital Market, said that the stock has started a series of higher highs and higher lows after hitting an all-time low around ₹100 on March 4, 2026. Going ahead, we advise traders to maintain a buy-on-dips approach and wait for a dip to add around the ₹155–₹160 levels. “On the higher side, 185 will act as immediate resistance. A decisive break above ₹185 could lead it towards its all-time highs,” he added. 
 
The company’s listed peers include Voltas, which is a likely market leader in the AC segment, followed by LG Electronics India, Blue Star, Havells through the Lloyd brand, and Johnson Controls-Hitachi
 
Notably, on Friday Voltas’ share price dipped over 3 per cent to hit an intraday low of ₹1,211 apiece, followed by a 2 per cent dip in Blue Star share price at ₹1,743 per share. Meanwhile, Havells’ share price also fell 1.4 per cent intraday. 
  
Disclaimer: Views and outlook in this report belong to the brokerages and analysts cited. They do not reflect the views of Business Standard. Readers are advised to exercise discretion.

data.title: India's GenAI course enrollments double in 2026 to 12 per min, says report
data.description:
India recorded 12 enrolments per minute in generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) courses in 2026, double the rate of six per minute in 2025, according to a report by Coursera.
 
The Global Skills Report 2026 said India ranked 40th globally and 12th in the Asia Pacific region in its new AI-Human Skills Synergy Index, which assesses how learners across 98 countries are developing artificial intelligence and human skills together.
 
The report combines learning data from more than 300 million Coursera and Udemy learners with Oxford Insights’ Government AI Readiness Index 2025 to assess countries’ AI and human skills development, alongside government capacity, policy infrastructure and technology readiness.
 
 
AI micro-credential enrolments in India rose 181 per cent year-on-year, exceeding global growth of 122 per cent, while overall AI course enrolments increased 57 per cent. The report also found that demand was shifting towards more specialised applications, with enrolments in AI security growing 296 per cent and those in agentic workflows rising 238 per cent.
 

Human skills learning trails global growth

 
The report, however, found that growth in human skills learning in India was slower than global benchmarks, highlighting the need to strengthen capabilities such as critical thinking, problem-solving and innovation alongside AI proficiency.
 
Enrolments in critical thinking courses in India increased 65 per cent year-on-year, compared with global growth of 107 per cent. Complex problem-solving enrolments rose 55 per cent against 126 per cent globally, while innovation-related learning grew 62 per cent, compared with 74 per cent worldwide.
 
The report said these capabilities would be important for workers to question AI-generated outputs, challenge assumptions, solve problems and make sound decisions.
 
“India has the scale and ambition to become a global hub for AI talent, building capabilities that serve both our economy and the world,” said Ashutosh Gupta, managing director, India and APAC, Coursera.
 
“India leads the world in AI learning on Coursera. Building on this momentum means deepening specialist and domain-specific AI expertise while strengthening the human skills that give our workforce a competitive edge. Investing in both will be essential to turning AI adoption into productivity and growth,” he added.
 

AI learning becomes more specialised

 
The report also found that AI learning was becoming more applied and specialised. Apart from AI security and agentic workflows, GenAI enrolments grew 125 per cent year-on-year. Trending skill areas included AI and machine learning foundations, large language model applications and modelling, and prompting and AI interaction.
 
Learners were also combining AI capabilities with communication and innovation skills. The report identified pairings such as prompting and AI interaction with communication and presentation, and AI workflows, integration and orchestration with innovation and ideation.

data.title: Jensen Huang excited about his 'second term' at Nvidia, says Trump
data.description:
By Josh Wingrove
 
President Donald Trump said Jensen Huang is looking forward to his “second term” as chief executive officer of Nvidia Corp., reiterating his praise for the man whose reinstatement he pushed hard for despite bipartisan backlash over national security concerns.
 
Speaking to reporters at his Mar-a-Lago club in Florida on Thursday, the president said he has not spoken to Huang since Nvidia announced his return, but probably will at some point.
 
“When I did speak to him, he is so happy to be going back. He calls it his second term,” Trump said.
 
The president again dismissed national security concerns over the reinstatement of Huang, who was ousted after revelations that he had extramarital affairs including with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy. 
 
 
“Based on information and belief, I think he’s absolutely fine,” Trump said. Pressed on what information he had, he did not give a specific answer, only saying, “The information I have, which is a lot of information.”
 
Nvidia earlier this week restored Huang as CEO, following intervention from Trump, who also enlisted Vice President JD Vance to help make a personal appeal to the board. Trump told CNBC on Monday he spoke to Nvidia’s board “directly and indirectly” and “felt very strongly” that Huang should be brought back.
 
Trump’s efforts drew widespread criticism from both Republicans and Democrats, with lawmakers vowing to investigate ties between Huang and the Trump administration. Huang is set to testify to House lawmakers behind closed doors on Dec. 1, and then publicly before the Senate on Dec. 3.
 
Nvidia’s stock soared more than 31% on Monday after the announcement of Huang’s return, but lost more than 9.5% in the next two days. The US market was closed on Thursday for the Thanksgiving holiday.
 
“I will tell you, the market feels very good about it,” Trump said. “I was a little concerned yesterday when I saw some pretty big dips, and by the end of the day, it was it was up again. So I really did, I think I did a great thing for our country and even for the world.”
 
Trump is due to travel on Dec. 4 to Arizona to headline a groundbreaking event for a Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Corp. chip manufacturing plant expansion — a facility that produces chips for Nvidia. 
 
The president said he hadn’t considered whether Huang should join him, but added: “I would be glad to take him.”

data.title: HSBC reorganizes support roles in India, impacts hundreds of jobs
data.description:
By Rthvika Suvarna, Saikat Das and Ambereen Choudhury
 
HSBC Holdings Plc is consolidating some support functions in India as the Asia-focused lender steps up efforts to rein in costs and accelerate the adoption of artificial intelligence. 
 
The bank recently told employees in India that it was centralizing finance functions across cities including Chennai, Gurugram and Bangalore and will no longer be housing those roles in other hubs, including Hyderabad and Pune, according to people with knowledge of the matter, who requested not to be named because the information is private.
 
The changes are confined to finance roles within HSBC’s so-called global capability centers in India, and employees expect the move to affect several hundred roles, according to the people. HSBC staff will be given the option and support to relocate, but the bank won’t provide further cash incentives for them to move, the people added.
  
HSBC has been weighing deep job cuts over the coming years as Chief Executive Officer Georges Elhedery deploys AI to shrink its middle and back offices. Non-client facing roles in global service centers are among those expected to be most impacted, people familiar have said previously. The changes could ultimately impact around 20,000 roles — or about 10% of its total workforce.
 
“As we simplify the bank, our focus remains on ensuring we have the right roles in the right locations to support the best customer outcomes,” an HSBC spokesperson said in a statement, referring to the roles in India. “We are taking the best of our people experience and combining this with emerging technologies to deliver outcomes that are better, faster, and safer for our clients.”
 
India has emerged as a key market for HSBC, alongside other major banks. HSBC describes itself as the largest foreign lender in the country and generated $1.9 billion of pretax profit in the region in 2025. It had about 47,000 employees in India at the end of last year. About 42,500 employees work in the global capability centers in India, including on technology, according to estimates from a person familiar with the matter.
 
Other banks have also been reshaping their Indian hubs, which have grown so large that Goldman Sachs Group Inc. and JPMorgan now employ more people in India than anywhere else outside the US. They are using AI to automate work such as checking loan documents, reconciling accounts and writing basic code, the same tasks that once gave fresh graduates their first jobs at those centers. 
 
Lenders globally are expecting AI to lead to fewer roles in the future. Standard Chartered Plc plans to cut close to 8,000 support roles over four years, while JPMorgan Chase & Co. CEO Jamie Dimon has said the technology will eliminate jobs broadly across industries. Banks are trimming junior analyst classes by as much as two-thirds, Debasish Patnaik, a senior partner at McKinsey & Co., said in June.
 
At HSBC, Elhedery has accelerated an overhaul of Europe’s largest bank through asset sales and operational simplification. 
 
In August, the lender said it expects its global restructuring effort to yield $2 billion in cost savings, up from an earlier target of $1.5 billion. The banker has made streamlining HSBC a central principle, saying earlier this year that he had been “ruthless about killing complexity” at the lender.

data.title: Mahanadi Coalfields set for stock market debut after $969 million IPO
data.description:
By Rajesh Mascarenhas
 
Mahanadi Coalfields Ltd., a unit of state-owned Coal India Ltd., is set to start trading Friday after its initial public offering in the first listing since India’s market regulator barred publishing so-called gray-market prices for IPO shares.
 
Indicative pre-listing prices have traditionally served as an informal benchmark for retail and wealthy investors seeking to gauge potential gains on the first day of trading. Several recent IPOs have made debuts at levels broadly in line with the prices in the unofficial market.
 
Mahanadi Coalfields, which raised ₹8,981 crore ($969 million) in the offer, will list on the exchanges 114 days after formally kicking off the IPO process on Aug. 5., ranking alongside companies taking the shortest time to go public. 
 
 
The IPO was subscribed 1.5 times when the bidding closed Monday, with institutions driving the demand. Qualified institutional buyers bid for 4.95 times the shares reserved for them, while portions allocated to other investor categories were undersubscribed, according to data published on the National Stock Exchange of India’s website.
 
The shares were priced at ₹136 apiece, the top end of the marketed range. The offering consisted entirely of shares sold by Coal India, with no fresh issuance, according to the prospectus.
 
At the IPO price, Mahanadi Coalfields offers a trailing dividend yield of 8.5%, compared to 6.6% for Coal India based on payouts for the year ended March, making the stock an attractive bet for cash returns, Prabhudas Lilladher Pvt. said in a note.
 
The price implies a 10% to 15% valuation premium for Mahanadi Coalfields over its parent, the brokerage said, adding that the unit’s superior operating profitability, return ratios and focused capital allocation justified this gap.
 
Still, Religare Broking Ltd. flagged in a note that declining returns and weakening operating metrics could weigh on the company’s financial performance despite its relatively strong position among peers, substantial coal reserves and an established customer base.

data.title: Festive season rush: Instant personal loan disbursals up 32% on Paisabazaar
data.description:
Instant personal loan disbursals facilitated through Paisabazaar rose 32% year-on-year during the festive season, with Maharashtra, Gujarat and Uttar Pradesh together accounting for more than a third of the platform’s total disbursals, according to the company’s latest data.
 
The increase points to continued demand for quick, digitally processed credit during a period when household spending typically rises. But the data also reveals a notable shift in the age profile of borrowers: consumers aged 46-55 are increasingly turning to instant personal loans.
 
Paisabazaar said disbursals in this age group grew 70% year-on-year during August, September and October 2026. Their share of total disbursals on the platform increased from 13% in the corresponding period of 2025 to 19% in 2026.
 
 
Borrowers aged 36-45 remained the largest segment, accounting for 40% of disbursals. Those aged 25-35 made up 36% of disbursals, with the segment recording 20% year-on-year growth.
 
The findings suggest that digital personal loans are not being used only by younger consumers. Established earners in their late forties and early fifties are also making greater use of such borrowing channels.
 
 Gujarat records fastest growth among top states
 
Maharashtra remained the largest state in terms of instant personal loan disbursals through Paisabazaar in 2026, followed by Gujarat and Uttar Pradesh.
 
Maharashtra recorded a 31% year-on-year increase in disbursals, while Gujarat saw growth of 57% and Uttar Pradesh 40%.
 
The top 10 states were Maharashtra, Gujarat, Uttar Pradesh, Telangana, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, Rajasthan, Delhi and Haryana.
 
The analysis compared personal loan disbursal data for August-October 2025 and August-October 2026 across more than 800 towns and cities in India.
 
Santosh Agarwal, chief executive officer of Paisabazaar, said the growth reflected the increasing convenience with which consumers could access credit through digital platforms.
 
The platform brings multiple lenders together and allows eligible borrowers to complete digital onboarding, compare available offers and proceed with an application.
 
Personal loan growth remains strong across the banking system
 
The platform-level increase comes against a backdrop of expanding personal credit in India.
 
According to the National Stock Exchange’s November 2026 *Market Pulse*, based on RBI data, bank personal loans grew 17.3% year-on-year in September 2026, compared with 11.5% a year earlier. The data covers the wider banking system and is not directly comparable with Paisabazaar’s festive-period disbursal figures.
 
The RBI’s August 2026 data showed personal loan outstanding at ₹72.9 lakh crore, with year-on-year growth of 16.9%. The expansion was supported by housing, vehicle loans and loans against gold jewellery, among other segments.
 
The shift towards younger borrowers is also visible in data from another digital lending platform. BharatLoan’s Data Report 2026 found that borrowers aged 25-30 accounted for 22.1% of its loan cases, up from 18% in 2025, while their share of loan value rose from 13% to 17.7%. The wider 25-35 age group made up 47.9% of BharatLoan’s loan cases, compared with 46.1% a year earlier. The report also found that women’s share of loan cases increased from 11.2% to 14.4%. 
 
 A caution on instant and unsecured credit
 
While digital platforms can make borrowing faster and easier, personal loans are generally unsecured and can carry relatively high interest rates compared with secured loans.
 
The Reserve Bank of India’s Financial Stability Report, published in 2026, noted that personal loans dominate consumption-related unsecured retail lending. The report also highlighted the growing role of fintech firms in small-ticket personal loans below ₹50,000.
 
Fintech firms accounted for 56.8% of this small-ticket segment by March 2026, with credit in the segment growing 41.6%. The RBI also flagged a 6.4% delinquency rate in the segment, indicating potential asset-quality risks. 
 
Consumers should compare the annual percentage rate, processing fee, total repayment amount, late-payment charges and prepayment terms before accepting an offer. A quick loan may help meet a genuine short-term need, but borrowing to fund discretionary festive spending can leave households with repayments long after the occasion has passed.

data.title: TVS family feud: What rights do daughters have over family business assets?
data.description:
Lakshmi Venu approached the Madras High Court on Wednesday, seeking partition of the joint family assets of the Venu Srinivasan branch of the TVS family. The move has brought the question of daughters’ inheritance rights in family-run businesses into focus.
 
The dispute concerns an arrangement reached within the family in 2024. While Venu Srinivasan maintains that the division was fair to both his children, Lakshmi and her mother, Mallika Srinivasan, are of the view that the division of business responsibilities did not settle their economic interests in the family assets.
 
The ownership structure adds another layer of complexity to the dispute. Interests in businesses such as TVS Holdings, TVS Motor Company, TVS Credit Services and Sundaram-Clayton are held through the VS Trust and other holding entities. The question now is whether the arrangements governing the allocation of assets within the family branch are legally valid.
 

Can daughters claim a share in family wealth during their father’s lifetime?

Yes, daughters can claim a share in the family’s wealth, depending on the nature of the property.
 
Section 6 of the Hindu Succession Act, 1956, recognises a daughter as a coparcener in a Hindu Mitakshara joint family. This means she acquires an equal right by birth in coparcenary property, just like a son. She can seek partition and is also subject to the same liabilities in respect of that property.
 
Coparcenary property refers to ancestral or joint family property held collectively by coparceners within a Hindu Undivided Family (HUF), in which eligible family members acquire a legal right by birth.
 
The Supreme Court, in Vineeta Sharma v. Rakesh Sharma, clarified that a daughter’s coparcenary rights do not depend on whether her father was alive when the amendment took effect. The right is acquired by birth, provided the coparcenary existed when the amendment came into force.

How does the law distinguish between ancestral and self-acquired business assets?

The distinction is based on the source of funding, lineage and whether the assets have been partitioned or merged with joint family property. The distinction is relevant under the Hindu Succession Act, 1956.
 
Ancestral or coparcenary property includes property inherited by a Hindu from ancestors under conditions recognised by Mitakshara law. Self-acquired property, on the other hand, includes assets purchased or developed by an individual using personal funds.
 
A father has the right to dispose of his self-acquired property at his discretion during his lifetime.
 
“The Supreme Court has consistently held that the mere existence of a joint Hindu family does not raise a presumption that its properties are joint family properties,” said Rishabh Gandhi, former judge and founder, Rishabh Gandhi and Advocates.
 
Property inherited under Section 8 of the Hindu Succession Act, 1956, does not ordinarily become coparcenary property in the hands of the heir, Gandhi added.

Can business assets held through family trusts be claimed in a partition suit?

Under Indian law, business assets held through a family trust generally cannot be directly partitioned in an ordinary partition suit, given the distinction between legal ownership and beneficial interests. Section 3 of the Indian Trusts Act, 1882, defines a trust as an obligation attached to the ownership of property.
 
“Private trusts are governed by the Indian Trusts Act, 1882. Its beneficiary rights include compelling the trustee to perform his duties and restraining a threatened breach of trust,” said Ray Vikram Nath, senior partner, Aretha Alpha.
 
Nath added that challenging the settlement of joint family property on the grounds that the settlor had no authority to alienate it rests on general principles of trust law rather than a specific judicial precedent cited in support of the argument. Such a legal challenge would be difficult to sustain, he said.

Is dividing management control the same as dividing ownership of family wealth?

No. Management and ownership are legally distinct concepts.
 
For instance, a family may decide that one child will manage a manufacturing business while another will look after a different business. Such an arrangement determines who runs the enterprise, but it does not establish ownership of the underlying assets or shares.
 
This distinction is important in the context of the March 2024 memorandum of understanding (MoU) signed by Venu Srinivasan, Mallika Srinivasan, Lakshmi and Sudarshan Venu. The arrangement is now a matter of dispute.
 
“Assigning operational control of different verticals to individual family members may settle day-to-day governance, but it does not by itself transfer underlying or beneficial value,” said Nitin Jain, partner, Agama Law Associates.
 
For a division of ownership to be durable, the transfer of economic interests must be formally documented and executed. An informal operational arrangement without corresponding ownership transfers remains vulnerable to challenge, Jain added.

Can an earlier family settlement prevent a daughter from seeking partition?

A valid family settlement is binding on its parties and prevents them from reopening matters that have already been resolved.
 
The Supreme Court, in Kale v. Deputy Director of Consolidation (1976), recognised the legal validity of bona fide family arrangements intended to resolve disputes and preserve harmony within the family.
 
“A daughter who signed can still challenge it for fraud, coercion, suppression of facts, or because it never actually settled her ownership. That is hard if she signed and took benefits, as estoppel then applies,” Nath added.

Can a family partition suit alter ownership and control of listed companies?

A partition suit does not transfer the assets of a listed company to individual family members.
 
Under company law, a company is a separate legal entity. Its assets belong to the company, while shareholders own shares that confer rights under the Companies Act, 2013, and the company’s articles.
 
The outcome of the TVS dispute will depend on the character of the assets, the trust arrangements and the validity of earlier settlements. “The court will now have to examine the earlier family agreements, the nature of the assets and whether Lakshmi's economic rights were actually settled,” said Alay Razvi, managing partner, Accord Juris.
 
“From a legal standpoint, the matter highlights the interplay between statutory inheritance rights, family settlement arrangements and the nature of asset ownership, particularly in multigenerational business families,” said Ankit Rajgarhia, partner, Bahuguna Law Associates.
